concern: 22 distinct mechanisms were tried on the same 217-assay panel, so the surviving result could in principle be a selection artefact; a protocol cannot 'nest' the choice of what to try
method: convert the paired bootstrap CI of the claim tier into an approximate standard error, then apply a two-sided Bonferroni correction for the number of attempts
verdict: the mechanism-selection concern is bounded to negligible. With 22 attempts the Bonferroni threshold is z = 3.05 and the observed effect is z = 5.16; the corrected 95% CI is [+0.00223, +0.00866], still entirely above zero. The claim would survive even if 10^5 configurations had been tried
caveat: Bonferroni assumes independence; the attempts here are correlated (many share components), which makes the correction conservative in our favour. The SE is derived from a bootstrap CI and assumes approximate normality of the resampling distribution
what_remains: an external panel is still the only way to confirm the effect on unseen assays; the multiplicity analysis bounds the selection risk but does not replace replication
